_comment: A NEGATIVE DIAGNOSTIC, NOT A PAPER RESULT. 2026-10-28.
The headline_curve campaign ran 22 SD3-Medium full-FT cells before the instance was deleted. Every one
returned attack success 0.00% at omega 7 -- including dirty_label, which is the positive control: 200 real
dog images captioned 'cat', a crude non-stealthy attack that MUST redirect something if the pipeline can
detect poisoning at all. It did not, so these 22 cells say nothing about H1 or H2.
Ruled out by inspection: data assembly is correct (dirty_label substitutes pair.target_anchor images under
source captions, verified in run_spec.py); poisoned ids are present (inputs.json lists 200); the poisons are
VAE-encoded fresh rather than read from the clean latent cache (the log shows 'vae 8/25' style progress);
the loader uses shuffle=True so poisons are not the tail that a 3200-microstep epoch drops; the judges were
validated separately on clean models with a positive control.
Remaining suspect: training strength. 800 optimizer steps x 4 accum = 3200 microsteps over 3400 images is
0.94 of an epoch, so each poison is seen about ONCE, at lr 1e-5 with cosine decay. The planned next step is
a single diagnostic cell at lr 1e-4 with everything else unchanged; if ASR moves, steps/lr must be re-pinned
and the whole campaign re-run. matrix.json pinned steps=800 to stop poison count from confounding with
training length, which is still the right instinct -- but 800 steps appears to sit below the threshold where
Authoritative per-cell records (config/inputs/metrics/evaluation + samples) were pushed to the private HF
dataset agasta/chimera-results as each cell finished. The numbers below were read off the box's
runner_log.json and per-run evaluation.json before the instance was deleted at 06:06:00 UTC.
_siglip_note: SigLIP read 0.00% on every one of the 22 cells, including the three where CLIP saw a single image.
